thread.title: Asian markets sink, with chip makers leading declines - MarketWatch

author: Ese Erheriene
title: Asian markets sink, with chip makers leading declines - MarketWatch
text:
Asia-Pacific stock markets pulled back on Friday after two days of broad gains, with a downbeat outlook from Taiwan Semiconductor prompting declines in technology names.
The company, one of the world’s biggest chip makers, expects second-quarter sales to come in more than 10% below analysts’ estimates, citing soft demand for high-end smartphones. The forecast sent the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down 4.3% Thursday in the U.S.
TSMC shares 2330, -6.34% fell 6.% on Friday, their worst day since 2013. The drop also pushed Taiwan’s benchmark Taiex stock index Y9999, -1.75% down 1.8% and pressured smartphone-component makers elsewhere in the region.
AAC 2018, -7.26% also slid 8.4% in Hong Kong, hitting an eight-month low, while lens maker Sunny Optical 2382, -5.63% declined 5.6%. In Japan, Tokyo Electron 8035, -2.05% fell 2.1% in the morning session, while South Korea’s Samsung 005930, -2.20% dropped 2.2%, with the wider Kospi Composite Index SEU, -0.39% off 0.4%.
The Shanghai Composite Index SHCOMP, -1.47% fell 1.5% and the Hang Seng HSI, -0.94% fell 0.7%.
Taiwan Semi’s warning resulted in “brewing concerns of weak iPhone demand,” weighing on Apple suppliers, noted Jingyi Pan, a market strategist at IG Group. Apple AAPL, -2.83% shares fell 2.8% on Thursday.
However, investors shouldn’t have broader concerns about Taiwan Semi’s forecast, said Oriano Lizza, a sales trader at CMC Markets. “I don’t see this being a long-term issue.”
“The trade-war impact is still in the market, and investors are still cautious,” said Castor Pang, head of research at Core Pacific-Yamaichi International. “With uncertainty ahead, investors will try and take profit before the weekend.”
Japan’s Nikkei NIK, -0.13% edged down 0.1%, in part supported by a small decline in the yen, which tends to boost shares of multinationals.
Elsewhere in markets, yields on 10 year-Treasurys TMUBMUSD10Y, +0.29% edged up to 2.922% Friday from 2.914% late Thursday, their highest settlement since February. Yields move inversely to prices.
Up ahead Friday is a meeting of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, where the potential to extend production caps may be discussed. Brent crude oil LCOM8, -0.61% was last down 0.3% at $73.57 a barrel after hitting 3 ½-year highs this week.
